rv.q: In the end, it’s Janney’s star turn that theatergoers will truly savor — and which makes 9 to 5 often feel like a 10!

Can this gaudy, empty musical really be part of the same Broadway season that gave us the minimally decorated, maximally effective “Exit the King,” “God of Carnage,” “Next to Normal,” “Hair,” “Mary Stuart” and “Norman Conquests”?

With many adjustments from the Broadway version, mainly set production quality, the downscaled play offers an array of well choreographed dance numbers, phenomenal musical scores from a live orchestra and colorful set changes and costumes....

Though the musical has some soaring heartfelt moments ("I Just Might," "Shine Like the Sun") and captures the lonely pangs of single women everywhere, this Broadway clunker does little to advance the lightweight material of the original. cn.t: Critics find this musical adaptation a gaudy, unexceptional retread of the film that fails to elevate its lightweight material, though strong performances and Dolly Parton's score provide occasional bright spots.

vs.sum: The Marquis Theatre offers excellent comfort with spacious seating and good sightlines from most areas, although the ambiance is somewhat lacking due to its modern, hotel-integrated design. Facilities are well-equipped with ample restrooms and concessions, making it a convenient choice for theatergoers.

acc.note: Elevator via Marriott Marquis hotel. 10 wheelchair spaces. No elevator to Mezzanine.
